summary: A cardholder makes a small purchase within the billing cycle, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario is designed to show timely satisfaction of the minimum payment obligation, preservation of the purchase grace period, and no late or over-limit fee outcome.
assumptions: The account starts this cycle with no previous balance, so the purchase grace-period condition applies under clause-6-grace-period.
The credit limit is $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario does not cause the outstanding balance to exceed that limit.
The periodic statement for this cycle shows a New Balance of $200.00 and a minimum payment of $15.00 (greater of 3% of $200.00 = $6.00 or $15.00).
The payment is made by an approved standard method and is credited on the date received.
No cash advances, returned payments, international transactions, disputed charges, or other fees occur in this scenario.

Because this is an on-time full-payment archetype, clause-4-credit-limit-obligation is satisfied by staying below the limit, clause-5-minimum-payment-obligation is satisfied by the payment before the due date, and clause-6-grace-period is represented by the issuer not imposing purchase interest during the grace period.

metadata.result: minimum paid on time; no late fee; no over-limit fee
